title: Tor against A/I^n of a finite module over a Noetherian ring is strictly pro-zero (Stacks 0911)
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I\subseteq A$ an ideal and $M$ a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. For $n\ge m\ge0$ let $\operatorname{Tor}^A_p(M,A/I^n)\to\operatorname{Tor}^A_p(M,A/I^m)$ be the map induced [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules] by the quotient map $A/I^n\to A/I^m$ (with $I^0=A$). Then for every $p>0$ there exists an integer $c>0$ such that the map $\operatorname{Tor}^A_p(M,A/I^n)\to\operatorname{Tor}^A_p(M,A/I^{n-c})$ is zero for all $n\ge c$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 0911 (lemma-tor-strictly-pro-zero, line 6449), with its proof (lines 6462--6473: p = 1 from 0 -> K -> A^t -> M -> 0, Tor_1(M, A/I^n) = (K cap (I^n)^t)/I^nK and Artin-Rees (Algebra, Lemma 00IN); p > 1 by dimension shifting); reference Quillen, Homology of commutative rings, Lemma 9.9. Tag verified in tags/tags: 0911,more-algebra-lemma-tor-strictly-pro-zero

proof.text: (Resolutions of $M$ and of $K$.) Let $M$ be a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Since $A$ is Noetherian, by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-free-resolution-noetherian] there is an exact complex $\cdots\to F_2\xrightarrow{d_2}F_1\xrightarrow{d_1}F_0\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}M\to0$ with $F_i=A^{\oplus n_i}$. Put $t=n_0$ and $K=\ker\varepsilon=\operatorname{im}d_1\subseteq A^{\oplus t}$, so that $0\to K\to A^{\oplus t}\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}M\to0$ is exact. $K$ is finitely generated, by the images under $d_1$ of the $n_1$ standard basis vectors of $F_1$. Let $d_1':F_1\to K$ be $d_1$ with target $K$; it is surjective, and $\ker d_1'=\ker d_1=\operatorname{im}d_2$, so $\cdots\to F_3\xrightarrow{d_3}F_2\xrightarrow{d_2}F_1\xrightarrow{d_1'}K\to0$ is exact: $G_q=F_{q+1}$ with differentials $d^G_q=d_{q+1}$ ($q\ge1$) is a resolution of $K$ by free modules. By [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], for every $A$-module $N$ we may and do compute $\operatorname{Tor}^A_p(M,N)=H_p(F_\bullet\otimes_AN)$ and $\operatorname{Tor}^A_q(K,N)=H_q(G_\bullet\otimes_AN)$ (another choice of resolution gives canonically isomorphic modules, Algebra 00LZ), and for an $A$-linear map $g:N\to N'$ the induced maps $\operatorname{Tor}_p(M,g)$, $\operatorname{Tor}_q(K,g)$ are the maps on homology induced by the maps of complexes $1\otimes g$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0911 (lemma-tor-strictly-pro-zero), lines 6462--6473 ('Choose a short exact sequence 0 -> K -> A^t -> M -> 0'); finite free resolution: Algebra, Lemma 00LP (lemma-resolution-by-finite-free); Tor computed from any free resolution: Algebra, Section 00LY and Lemma 00LZ (lemma-tor-welldefined)

proof.text: (Dimension shifting, natural in $N$.) Let $p\ge2$ and $N$ an $A$-module, with the resolutions of Step 1. In $F_\bullet\otimes_AN$, $H_p=\ker(d_p\otimes1_N:F_p\otimes N\to F_{p-1}\otimes N)/\operatorname{im}(d_{p+1}\otimes1_N)$. Since $p-1\ge1$, $F_p=G_{p-1}$, $F_{p-1}=G_{p-2}$, $F_{p+1}=G_p$, $d_p=d^G_{p-1}$ and $d_{p+1}=d^G_p$ (for $p=2$: $d_2=d^G_1:G_1=F_2\to G_0=F_1$), so $H_p(F_\bullet\otimes_AN)$ and $H_{p-1}(G_\bullet\otimes_AN)$ are the same quotient of the same submodule of $F_p\otimes_AN$. Hence $\operatorname{Tor}^A_p(M,N)=\operatorname{Tor}^A_{p-1}(K,N)$ [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. For $g:N\to N'$ both $\operatorname{Tor}_p(M,g)$ and $\operatorname{Tor}_{p-1}(K,g)$ are induced by the same map $1_{F_p}\otimes g:F_p\otimes N\to F_p\otimes N'$, so under these identifications $\operatorname{Tor}_p(M,g)=\operatorname{Tor}_{p-1}(K,g)$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0911 (lemma-tor-strictly-pro-zero), lines 6462--6473 ('For p > 1 we have Tor_p(M, A/I^n) = Tor_{p-1}(K, A/I^n)'), here read off the resolution of Step 1 instead of the long exact sequence

proof.text: ($\operatorname{Tor}_1$ against $A/J$.) Let $J\subseteq A$ be an ideal. For every $A$-module $X$, $X\otimes_A(A/J)\cong X/JX$, $x\otimes\bar a\mapsto ax\bmod JX$, naturally in $X$ [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring] (1) (with the symmetry of $\otimes$); for ideals $J\subseteq J'$ the map induced by the quotient $A/J\to A/J'$ becomes the reduction $X/JX\to X/J'X$ (both send $x\otimes\bar a$ to $ax\bmod J'X$). So $F_\bullet\otimes_A(A/J)$ is the complex $F_i/JF_i$ with differentials $\bar d_i$, and $\operatorname{Tor}^A_1(M,A/J)=\ker(\bar d_1:F_1/JF_1\to A^{\oplus t}/JA^{\oplus t})/\operatorname{im}\bar d_2$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] applied to the exact sequence $F_2\xrightarrow{d_2}F_1\xrightarrow{d_1'}K\to0$ of Step 1 and to $A/J$, the sequence $F_2/JF_2\xrightarrow{\bar d_2}F_1/JF_1\xrightarrow{\bar d_1'}K/JK\to0$ is exact. Let $\bar\iota:K/JK\to A^{\oplus t}/JA^{\oplus t}$ be induced by the inclusion $K\subseteq A^{\oplus t}$; then $\bar d_1=\bar\iota\circ\bar d_1'$. Hence $\ker\bar d_1=(\bar d_1')^{-1}(\ker\bar\iota)$ contains $\ker\bar d_1'=\operatorname{im}\bar d_2$ and maps onto $\ker\bar\iota$ ($\bar d_1'$ is surjective), so $\bar d_1'$ induces an isomorphism $\theta_J:\operatorname{Tor}^A_1(M,A/J)\xrightarrow{\sim}\ker\bar\iota$. As $JA^{\oplus t}=J^{\oplus t}$ and $JK\subseteq K\cap J^{\oplus t}$, $\ker\bar\iota=\{k+JK:\ k\in K\cap J^{\oplus t}\}=(K\cap J^{\oplus t})/JK$. For $J\subseteq J'$ all maps above commute with the reductions mod $J'$, so $\theta_{J'}\circ\operatorname{Tor}_1(M,A/J\to A/J')\circ\theta_J^{-1}$ is the map $(K\cap J^{\oplus t})/JK\to(K\cap J'^{\oplus t})/J'K$, $k+JK\mapsto k+J'K$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0911 (lemma-tor-strictly-pro-zero), lines 6462--6473 ('Then Tor_1^A(M, A/I^n) = K cap (I^n)^t / I^n K', stated without proof; written out here)

proof.text: (The case $p=1$.) Let $M$, $t$, $K$ be as in Step 1. $A^{\oplus t}$ is a finitely generated $A$-module and $K\subseteq A^{\oplus t}$ a submodule, $A$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], so by the Artin--Rees lemma [lem-weil-pbc-artin-rees] (with $R=A$, its $M=A^{\oplus t}$, its $N=K$) there is $c_0\ge0$ such that $I^nA^{\oplus t}\cap K\subseteq I^{n-c}K$ for all $n\ge c$, for every $c\ge c_0$ (the 'in particular' clause of that node). Take $c=\max(c_0,1)>0$; note $I^nA^{\oplus t}=(I^n)^{\oplus t}$. Let $n\ge c$ and $m=n-c\ge0$ ($I^0=A$), so $I^n\subseteq I^m$. By Step 3 (with $J=I^n$, $J'=I^m$) an element of $\operatorname{Tor}^A_1(M,A/I^n)$ is $\theta_{I^n}^{-1}(k+I^nK)$ with $k\in K\cap(I^n)^{\oplus t}$, and its image in $\operatorname{Tor}^A_1(M,A/I^m)$ is $\theta_{I^m}^{-1}(k+I^mK)$. Since $k\in K\cap(I^n)^{\oplus t}\subseteq I^{n-c}K=I^mK$, this image is $0$. So $\operatorname{Tor}^A_1(M,A/I^n)\to\operatorname{Tor}^A_1(M,A/I^{n-c})$ is zero for all $n\ge c$, with $c>0$ depending only on $M$ (through $K\subseteq A^{\oplus t}$) and $I$, uniform in $n$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0911 (lemma-tor-strictly-pro-zero), lines 6462--6473 ('By Artin-Rees (Algebra, Lemma 00IN) there is a constant c >= 0 such that K cap (I^n)^t subset I^{n-c}K for n >= c. Thus the result for p = 1'); Artin-Rees: Algebra, Lemma 00IN (lemma-Artin-Rees, line 12187)

proof.text: (Induction on $p$.) Fix $A$ and $I$. Claim $P(p)$ for $p\ge1$: for every finitely generated $A$-module $M$ there is $c>0$ such that $\operatorname{Tor}^A_p(M,A/I^n)\to\operatorname{Tor}^A_p(M,A/I^{n-c})$ is zero for all $n\ge c$. $P(1)$ is Step 4. Let $p\ge2$ and assume $P(p-1)$. Given $M$, let $K$ be as in Step 1; it is finitely generated, so $P(p-1)$ gives $c>0$ with $\operatorname{Tor}^A_{p-1}(K,A/I^n)\to\operatorname{Tor}^A_{p-1}(K,A/I^{n-c})$ zero for all $n\ge c$. By Step 2 with $N=A/I^n$, $N'=A/I^{n-c}$ and $g$ the quotient map, $\operatorname{Tor}_p(M,g)=\operatorname{Tor}_{p-1}(K,g)$ under the identifications $\operatorname{Tor}^A_p(M,-)=\operatorname{Tor}^A_{p-1}(K,-)$, hence $\operatorname{Tor}_p(M,g)=0$ for all $n\ge c$, and $P(p)$ holds with the same $c$. By induction $P(p)$ holds for all $p\ge1$, which is the statement.

No new nodes. The citer lem-weil-pbc-limit-flat-modules uses only p = 1, consistent with Step 4. Mathlib: no match (five searches added).
